why: For part (b), the student compares the do-while with a plain while loop, which is code that isn't given, and names the inputs where they behave differently (a start below 70, which includes 61). That correct reasoning about a change is L4, even though the answer never gives the exact output for 61, which would be "61 ".

concepts.quote: With a while loop the output is the same here, because 81 >= 70 is true at the start; it would only differ if i started below 70.
concepts.why: A while loop tests before its first pass, so it runs zero times when i starts below 70; the do-while runs once and prints 61, so the student's rule is right.
The student works out the loop condition correctly with the starting value 81.
